name: Fetch (what to retrieve from STEP, and when)

meta.purpose: Decide WHAT the study pulls and WHEN. Which terms, which of their relations, on what trigger, and to what depth. This process decides how much of Scripture's evidence the study ever sees — everything downstream can only analyse what fetch chose to retrieve.
meta.why_it_carries_the_completeness_risk: Every other layer's failure is visible in what it produced. Fetch's failure is invisible by construction: a term never pulled leaves no gap, no null, no flag — just an absence nothing can point at. The two prior ~100-page studies failed by UNDERSTATING the inner being, and this is the process where understating begins.
meta.envelope: Every item carries the common rule envelope — see ../_manifest.json meta.envelope.

boundary.util.step: HOW STEP is reached and what it can do — endpoints, connection, the cap, the response components. Cited here, never restated.
boundary.fetch (this file): WHAT to retrieve and WHEN — scope, relations, triggers, depth.
boundary.raw: WHAT IS STORED and its controls — immutability, source-precedence, no duplication.

meta.state: PARTIAL — authored 2026-07-15 to home the researcher's related-term ruling. Strong's resolution, worklist definition, and retry policy are stubs pending their own pass.

the_related_term_problem.the_researcher_framing: 'Not every related term is relevant, but we do not know which are relevant without looking into them. Not pulling the related terms potentially compromises the completeness of the study.' (2026-07-15)
the_related_term_problem.why_this_is_hard: Both choices lose. Pull everything and the study explodes in scope — one word (worship) named 666 related words across 36 terms, most irrelevant. Pull nothing and relevance is decided by NOT LOOKING, which is not a judgement, it is an omission. There is no cheap correct answer, only a chosen risk.
the_related_term_problem.the_ruling: The DEFAULT is not to pull all related terms and verses. But the OPTION must exist, and when taken it must pull and process using the SAME METHODS AND CONTROLS. Relevance stays a decision that CAN be made from evidence, rather than one foreclosed by the pipeline.
the_related_term_problem.what_this_is_really_saying: The default is a COST decision, not a truth claim. Nothing in the config may read the default as 'related terms do not matter' — it says only 'we are not pulling them today'. That distinction is the whole point: an omission the study knows about is a debt; one it has forgotten is a false result.
the_related_term_problem.the_asymmetry_that_decides_it: A false positive (pulling an irrelevant term) costs disk and a screening decision. A false negative (never pulling a relevant one) is invisible forever and understates the inner being. The costs are not comparable, which is why the option must exist even though the default is off.

nodes.process: What is fetched, when, and to what depth — including the related-term option and the mitigation that carries the default.
nodes.entities: None of its own. Fetch retrieves; raw stores.
nodes.output: The fetch report — including what was NOT pulled.

open.issue: The default relies on fetch.candidate-triggers-pull: a span in an already-pulled verse gets marked a candidate characteristic, which triggers pulling its term. The researcher named this explicitly as 'not fool proof'. This open states exactly WHERE it is blind, so the blindness is a known quantity rather than a hope.
open.the_blind_spot: The cascade can only ever see terms that CO-OCCUR with a verse the study has already pulled. A related term whose occurrences fall entirely in verses no registered term touches is INVISIBLE TO IT — permanently. It is not found late; it is never found. The mitigation's reach is bounded by the corpus the study has already chosen, so it can deepen coverage but can never extend it beyond that boundary.
open.who_it_misses_specifically: Exactly the terms most worth finding: an inner-being word the registry never thought of, occurring in passages the registry's words do not reach. The mitigation is strongest where the study is already looking and weakest where it is blind — which is the wrong way round.
open.why_it_still_carries_the_default: It is not nothing. Most related terms of an inner-being word DO co-occur with it, so the cascade catches the dense middle cheaply. It is a good default precisely because the expensive option exists for the rest.
options: A: accept the blind spot; the related-term option is the escape hatch when a book or cluster warrants it (the ruling as it stands)
B: periodically run the related-term option corpus-wide as an AUDIT — not to ingest everything, but to MEASURE what the default is missing, then decide

C: use STEP route A (English text search — step.route-semantics) as an independent check: A \ (B u C) is exactly 'English inner-being words with no registered Strong's', which is the same blind spot approached from the other side
open.recommendation: A as the operating rule, plus C as the periodic check. C is the natural fit — the route model already computes this set difference, it is cheap, and it finds the misses the cascade structurally cannot, because it does not start from the study's existing corpus. That is precisely the independent witness the blind spot needs.
open.resolve_by: researcher decision — not urgent, but it is the only measure of what the default costs

open.issue: When fetch.include-related is ON, related terms are pulled with verses and meaning. But related terms have related terms. Is the pull one level deep, or transitive?
open.consequence: Transitive closure over a 666-related-word graph is unbounded. One level is arbitrary but finite.
open.recommendation: ONE LEVEL, and record that the boundary was drawn. Transitivity turns a scoped pull into a crawl of the lexicon, and the second level's relevance is already vanishing. If a second-level term matters, its first-level parent will have been onboarded and the option can be taken again from there — which is bounded, deliberate, and leaves a record.
open.resolve_by: researcher decision — needed before the option is first used

process.subject: related-term-inclusion
process.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15: 'the code must include the option to pull a term and all its related terms verses and terms meaning. The default is to not include all related terms and verses, but it may be required, and then the option must exist to pull and process using the same methods and controls.'
process.intent: Make related-term depth a CHOICE the researcher makes per run, not a limit the code imposes. The default is off for cost; the option exists because relevance cannot be known without looking.
process.satisfaction: The option exists, defaults to off, is settable per run, and when on pulls related terms through the identical pipeline.

spec.scope: per run — overridable at launch; the default lives in config
spec.when_false: Pull the main term only: its term, meaning, related-term NAMES, and its verses with spans. Related terms are recorded as named relations, NOT as evidence. The mitigation (fetch.candidate-triggers-pull) carries discovery.
spec.when_true: Additionally pull, FOR EVERY RELATED TERM NAMED: its term, its meaning, and its verses with spans — the full component set (step.response-validation), through the same fetch, the same gates, the same raw controls.
spec.⚠ the_default_is_a_cost_decision_not_a_t: OFF does not mean related terms are irrelevant. It means the study has not looked yet. Nothing downstream may treat an unpulled related term as evidence of absence — that would convert a budget decision into a finding (step.is-a-source-not-the-truth applies with equal force to our own omissions).
spec.why_a_setting_and_not_a_rule: The right depth is not a property of the method, it is a property of the QUESTION. A book being read at span depth may warrant it; a broad sweep will not. Config exists so that judgement stays with the researcher instead of being frozen into code.

process.subject: fetch-uniform-controls
process.authority: researcher ruling 2026-07-15: 'the option must exist to pull and process using the same methods and controls'
process.intent: Guarantee there is no second-class pull. A related term retrieved under the option is retrieved exactly as a main term is — same endpoints, same completeness arithmetic, same validation, same raw controls.
process.satisfaction: No fetch path exists that bypasses any control a main-term fetch passes.

spec.statement: ONE pipeline. A related-term pull uses the same methods and the same controls as a main-term pull. There is no 'quick side pull'.
spec.what_it_forbids: A convenience path that fetches related terms without the oracle check, without span validation, without step-precedence, or without the response-component gate. Data acquired outside the controls is data nothing can vouch for — and it would sit in the same tables as data that can, indistinguishably.
the_controls_that_apply_identically: gate.step.available — the pre-flight (raw processes do not run without it)
gate.step.api-fit — no raw sourced from English-text search
raw.step-precedence — a re-pull validates; STEP wins on difference
raw.no-duplication — one live row per identity
spec.why_this_is_a_rule_and_not_an_assumption: This is exactly where a shortcut is tempting — 666 related words is a lot to put through the full battery, and the pressure to 'just grab the glosses' is real. The failure record calls this pattern point-solutions: a side path built under time pressure that quietly becomes the main path. Naming it as red closes it.
spec.the_corollary: Because the controls are identical, a related term pulled under the option is INDISTINGUISHABLE from one onboarded directly — which is correct. It IS a term. The option is about WHETHER to look, never about how well.

process.subject: candidate-triggered-fetch
process.authority: researcher 2026-07-15: 'The verses include span that potentially could be marked as a candidate characteristic, which would then trigger pulling the term with its verses if it does not already exist in the study.'
process.intent: Carry discovery when fetch.include-related is off. A pulled verse contains OTHER spans; any of them may be marked a candidate characteristic; a candidate whose term the study does not hold triggers that term's pull.
process.satisfaction: Every candidate-marked span resolves to a term the study holds — pulling it if it does not.

spec.statement: A span marked candidate-characteristic in a pulled verse TRIGGERS a pull of its term (with verses and meaning) if the study does not already hold it. The pull uses the same methods and controls (fetch.same-controls).
spec.why_it_works: The study's verses are dense with inner-being vocabulary. A term genuinely in the inner-being neighbourhood of a registered word very often OCCURS ALONGSIDE it — so reading the verse surfaces it for free, without pulling 666 relations. This is discovery through evidence rather than through the lexicon.
spec.its_relationship_to_the_registry: This is the `discovery` layer of char.seed-layers, given a fetch trigger. The seed is deliberately over-inclusive; this is how over-inclusion reaches terms the registry never named.
spec.⚠ NOT_FOOLPROOF: Named as such by the researcher, and the limit is structural, not incidental: the cascade can only ever see terms that CO-OCCUR with an already-pulled verse. A related term occurring only where no registered term appears is invisible to it — permanently, not merely late. See open.fetch.mitigation-blind-spot.
spec.the_honest_summary: It deepens the corpus the study already has. It cannot widen it. fetch.include-related is what widens it — which is why the option must exist.

process.subject: fetch-omission
process.authority: derived 2026-07-15 from the related-term ruling; plan §1.2 ('coverage was a mirage')
process.intent: Keep what the study chose not to pull VISIBLE, so a scope decision can never be mistaken for a finding of absence.
process.satisfaction: Every run records what it did not fetch and why; no analysis treats an unfetched term as absent.

spec.statement: What was NOT pulled is recorded — the related terms named but not fetched, the depth not taken, the setting that governed. An omission the study knows about is a debt. An omission it has forgotten is a false result.
spec.why_red: This is the ONLY defence against fetch's invisible failure mode. Every other layer's gaps are visible as nulls or flags; an unfetched term leaves nothing at all. If the omission is not written down at the moment of the decision, it cannot be reconstructed afterwards — there is no trace to find.
spec.connects: The lexical layer already enforces this distinction as assess-never-absent: 'assessed and found nothing' is a finding, 'never assessed' is a defect. The same rule at the fetch boundary — and it matters more here, because fetch's silence is the earliest and the most total.

output.subject: fetch-report
output.intent: Report what a fetch retrieved AND what it deliberately did not — the second being the part nothing else can reconstruct.
output.satisfaction: Every fetch run reports pulled terms, their component completeness, and the named-but-not-pulled set with the setting that governed.

must_include: terms pulled, with rows-vs-oracle per term
RELATED TERMS NAMED BUT NOT PULLED — with the include-related setting that governed
candidate-triggered pulls (what the mitigation caught this run)
STEP gaps (attested by the master, untagged by STEP)
spec.the_important_section_is_the_second: A fetch report that lists only what it fetched is a receipt. The value is the not-pulled set: it is the study's own record of the risk it accepted, at the moment it accepted it.

validation.subject: fetch-uniform-controls
validation.intent: Refuse any fetch that reached raw without passing every control a main-term fetch passes.
validation.satisfaction: Every raw row's provenance shows the full control set was applied, whatever triggered its pull.

spec.note: A pull's TRIGGER is provenance worth keeping — it says why the study holds this term. It is never a reason to apply different controls.

validation.subject: candidate-triggered-fetch
validation.intent: Catch a candidate-marked span whose term the study does not hold — the trigger that makes the default's discovery work.
validation.satisfaction: No candidate-marked span references a term absent from the study.

spec.on_fail: trigger the term's pull; halt only if the pull itself fails
spec.relationship_to_I2: char.candidate-requires-verse-record is the same shape one layer up — a candidate must resolve to a verse-record. This is: a candidate must resolve to a TERM THE STUDY HOLDS. Both say a candidate cannot point at nothing.

validation.subject: fetch-omission
validation.intent: Refuse a fetch that does not record what it left behind.
validation.satisfaction: Every fetch records its named-but-not-pulled set and the governing setting.

spec.why_red: Fetch is the one layer whose failure leaves no trace. Recorded at the time or lost forever — there is no later audit that can recover a decision nobody wrote down.
